lead: >-
  In our selection of event-focused trips that include Chile, the celebrations usually take place outside Chile itself: New Year's Eve on Copacabana Beach in Rio de Janeiro, the Carnival Champions' Parade at the Sambadrome, or, on one itinerary, a New Year's celebration in Buenos Aires. After the main event, the journey continues to Chile, taking in Santiago, wine valleys, the Atacama Desert or Patagonia. We compare seven available multi-country itineraries, their holiday dates, included tickets and the number of days actually spent in Chile.
---

## Events and festivals on tours that include Chile: where the celebrations take place

**Choose this collection if you want to combine Rio Carnival or a New Year's trip with a visit to Chile.** Our catalogue features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} whose itineraries include Chile and are tagged for events and festivals. However, the currently confirmed itineraries do not indicate that travellers will attend a festival **in Chile itself**. The main celebrations on these trips take place in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) or [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/).

This distinction matters when choosing a trip. The celebrations often occupy one night or several days at the start of the journey, followed by [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), Argentina, [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), the [Atacama Desert](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) and other countries. Consider the date and details of the main event, whether tickets are included, additional flights and the time available in each country.

| Event | Where it takes place on the tour |
|---|---|
| New Year's Eve on Copacabana | Rio, Brazil |
| Carnival and the Champions' Parade | Rio, Brazil |
| New Year's Eve with a tango show | Buenos Aires, Argentina |

Chile has its own annual festivals, too. For example, the national *Fiestas Patrias* celebrations take place in September, while the La Tirana festival is held in northern Chile in July. However, **neither attendance at Fiestas Patrias nor participation in La Tirana is listed as an included activity on these seven tours**. If a Chilean festival is the main reason for your trip, you will need different dates and an appropriate itinerary; the event-focused label on this catalogue does not guarantee one. For an overview of the country's geography and seasons, see our [Chile guide](/chile/).

## New Year 2027: celebrating on Copacabana and travelling to Santiago

The [10-day New Year's tour of Brazil, Argentina and Chile](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-new-year-2027-10-days/) runs from **30 December 2026 to 8 January 2027**. The main celebration takes place on 31 December on Copacabana Beach in Rio. Travellers then visit both sides of Iguazu Falls, continue to Buenos Aires for an evening tango show and finish their journey in Chile. The final days are spent in [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), with a city sightseeing tour on 7 January.

The [11-day "New Year's Fairy Tale: Brazil, Argentina and Chile"](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-new-year-11-days-2027/) also begins on **30 December 2026**, but ends on 9 January 2027. It includes four nights in Rio, with a free day after New Year's Eve, followed by Iguazu, Buenos Aires and Santiago. Exploring the Chilean capital is scheduled for 8 January; a visit to the [Maipo Valley](/chile/place/maipo-valley/) is described as an **optional** activity, not a guaranteed included excursion.

The two tours differ in length and the amount of free time. Both suit travellers who want to enjoy New Year's Eve in Rio before discovering Chile's capital, rather than spend the holiday specifically in Santiago. It is also important to distinguish the public celebration on Copacabana from a paid hotel party or dinner: the 11-day itinerary lists a special dinner separately as an optional extra.

For a longer journey, consider the [19-day New Year's itinerary across five countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-new-year-group-tour-19-days/). After celebrating in Rio, it travels through Argentina and Chile, then Bolivia and Peru. The Chilean portion includes [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) and the start of the journey towards [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/); the subsequent high-altitude stops and the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) are already in Bolivia. This trip requires considerably more time than the 10- or 11-day options ending in Santiago.

## Rio Carnival and the Champions' Parade: how Chile fits into the itinerary

Carnival is the main reason to choose several of the following tours. The [Sambadrome and Rio Carnival](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) are in **Brazil**, however. On these trips, Chile comes later, after the festivities, the waterfalls and Buenos Aires.

On the [19-day "Highlights of Five Countries" tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-carnival-private-tour/), an evening visit to the Sambadrome is scheduled for the opening days, with transfers to and from the parade mentioned in the itinerary. After Rio, the route takes in Iguazu and [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), followed by a flight to [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) and a journey to the [Atacama Desert](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The trip continues through Bolivia and Peru. It is an option for travellers who want to explore several Andean regions after Carnival rather than spend the rest of the holiday on the beach.

The [18-day "Five Countries with the Champions' Parade"](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/) is built around a different event: the final performance by the best samba schools. After the festive evening, the itinerary visits the Brazilian and Argentine sides of [Iguazu](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), then Buenos Aires, Santiago, Atacama, Bolivia and Peru. Here it is especially important to check which evening is specified and how the subsequent travel is arranged: the regular competitive parades and the Champions' Parade take place on different dates and are different events.

There is also the [10-day "Champions' Parade, Tango and Wine" tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-champions-parade-10-days-2027/). It combines the Champions' Parade in Rio with Iguazu and a tango show with dinner in Buenos Aires, ending in Santiago. **A Carnival ticket and return transfers between the hotel and the Sambadrome are included** in this itinerary. A trip to the wine-producing [Maipo Valley](/chile/place/maipo-valley/) is listed separately as optional. This is an important distinction: a reference to "wine" in the title does not automatically mean that tastings are included.

For reference, according to the published **2027 Carnival schedule, the Champions' Parade is planned for 13 February**, following the main competitive evenings on 7–9 February. The 10-day tour listing gives a provisional travel period of 12–21 February 2027. Before paying, it is therefore essential to match the actual ticket date to the appropriate day of the itinerary and the order of visits across the three countries. Festival schedules may change, and a tour title is no substitute for checking the specific admission ticket.

## A different itinerary: New Year's Eve in Argentina, Chile earlier in the trip

The [18-day "Argentina, Chile, Bolivia and Patagonia" itinerary](/multi-country/tour/argentina-chile-bolivia-cruise-tour-18-days/) is very different from the Copacabana New Year's tours. **Chile is visited before New Year's Eve**: first [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), then Atacama and a journey into Bolivia towards Uyuni. After returning to Chile, the route visits [Puerto Natales and Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/) and includes a cruise from [Punta Arenas](/chile/place/punta-arenas/) through the southern straits and fjords.

According to the published itinerary, the night of 31 December is spent **in Buenos Aires**, with a tango show and dinner. This tour therefore suits travellers looking to combine a South American cruise and Patagonian landscapes with a New Year's celebration in Argentina. It does not promise a celebration in Chile and is not equivalent to a short New Year's trip to Rio. The itinerary mentions travel from 20 December to 6 January; the year, cruise availability and sailing dates need to be checked when choosing a departure.

If Patagonia itself is your primary interest rather than the holiday evening, compare [cruises and expeditions that visit Chile](/interests/cruises-and-expeditions/tours/chile/). The presence of a cruise does not mean the itinerary dates can be freely rearranged: departures, domestic flights and connections determine the sequence of the entire journey.

## Comparing the seven available itineraries

| Tour | Event and Chilean portion |
|---|---|
| [New Year, 10 days](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-new-year-2027-10-days/) | Copacabana; Santiago at the end |
| [New Year's Fairy Tale, 11 days](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-new-year-11-days-2027/) | Copacabana; Santiago, optional Maipo |
| [New Year, five countries, 19 days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-new-year-group-tour-19-days/) | Copacabana; Santiago, Atacama |
| [Carnival, five countries, 19 days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-carnival-private-tour/) | Sambadrome; Santiago, Atacama |
| [Champions' Parade, five countries, 18 days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/) | Rio; Santiago, Atacama |
| [Champions' Parade, 10 days](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-champions-parade-10-days-2027/) | Ticket in Rio; Santiago |
| [Argentina, Chile, Bolivia, 18 days](/multi-country/tour/argentina-chile-bolivia-cruise-tour-18-days/) | New Year's Eve in Buenos Aires; Patagonia |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_tur_v_braziliyu_argentinu_i_chili_na_novyj_god,tour_brazil_argentina_chile_new_year_11_days_2027,tour_source_5_stran_latinskoj_ameriki_na_16_dnej_na_novyj_god,tour_source_karnaval_5_stran,tour_source_5_stran_latinskoj_ameriki_i_parad_chempionov_karnavala,tour_brazil_argentina_chile_champions_parade_10_days_2027,tour_source_kruiznyj_tur_po_luchshim_mestam_argentiny_chili_i_bolivii}}

The table shows the current names, durations and available pricing details of these itineraries. Sharing the same celebration date does not make trips interchangeable: one may include several free days, another flights between three countries, and a third continues above an altitude of 3,000 metres.

## Checking tickets, itineraries and prices before booking

Before choosing an event-focused tour, compare **four things**. First, identify the exact festive evening: a competitive Carnival parade, the Champions' Parade or New Year's Eve. Second, check whether admission is included, whether transfers are provided and what category of seat is offered. Third, consider how much time is spent travelling between Rio, Iguazu, Buenos Aires and Santiago. Fourth, distinguish excursions in Chile that are guaranteed by the itinerary from those offered as optional extras.

Do not assume that the terms of one tour apply to another. The [10-day Champions' Parade tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-champions-parade-10-days-2027/) lists admission to the show as included; the [11-day New Year's trip](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-new-year-11-days-2027/) lists a special hotel dinner as optional. Also check domestic flights: having three countries in the tour's name does not automatically tell you which flights are covered by the price.

Finally, consider the season. New Year's Eve falls during the Southern Hemisphere summer and Carnival takes place in February, but conditions in [central Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) and [southern Patagonia](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/) differ greatly. When travelling via [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), discuss altitude, acclimatisation and the pace of excursions separately. Plan the Chilean portion around its own geography, not simply around the holiday calendar of a neighbouring country.

## Frequently asked questions about holiday tours that visit Chile

### Do any of the seven current itineraries include a festival in Chile itself?

The confirmed festive events take place in Brazil and Argentina. In Chile, the tours visit [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), Atacama or Patagonia. Chile's Fiestas Patrias and La Tirana may provide reasons for a separate journey, but neither event is included in these itineraries.

### Which tour should I choose to celebrate New Year's Eve and then visit Chile?

For a shorter introduction, choose the [10-day New Year's itinerary](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-new-year-2027-10-days/), which finishes in Santiago. The [11-day option](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-new-year-11-days-2027/) allows more time, while the [19-day five-country itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-new-year-group-tour-19-days/) continues through Atacama, Bolivia and Peru.

### Where does the Carnival Champions' Parade take place?

At the Sambadrome in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). Event-focused itineraries that also visit Chile include a [10-day tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-champions-parade-10-days-2027/) and an [18-day five-country tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/). Check the parade date and confirmed ticket for your particular departure.

### Are excursions in Chile and visits to wineries included in every holiday tour?

No. For example, some programmes offer the [Maipo Valley](/chile/place/maipo-valley/) as an optional excursion. A standard Santiago city tour and an additional winery excursion are different services. Each itinerary specifies what is included.

### Can I choose a Chilean festival instead of Carnival?

Yes. Chile hosts national and regional celebrations, but finding suitable dates and visits requires a separate itinerary. None of the seven current event-focused tours confirms attendance at a Chilean festival. For a journey without a festive date, consider the [general Chile tour catalogue](/chile/tour/) or [cultural itineraries in Chile](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/chile/).

lead: >-
  Our Ecuador events collection includes an 11-day New Year's tour from 30 December 2026 to 9 January 2027. The group celebrates in Quito with local traditions and a festive dinner, then travels through the Andes via Quilotoa, Baños, Chimborazo and Cuenca before continuing to the Galápagos Islands. The celebration takes one evening; the rest of the journey explores culture, volcanoes and wildlife. Here we examine the schedule, guide arrangements, flights to the islands and what is included in the price.
---

## New Year in Ecuador: the Ada Tours itinerary

Our themed catalogue offers {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The current festive itinerary is ["All of Ecuador for New Year: the Andes and Galápagos"](/ecuador/tour/complete-ecuador-new-year/). It is an **11-day, 10-night group tour from 30 December 2026 to 9 January 2027**. The main celebration takes place in [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/), with sightseeing scheduled for 31 December followed by a New Year's dinner with music and dancing.

**If you want to celebrate New Year the Ecuadorian way and then discover the Andes and the Galápagos, this tour fits that plan.** The celebrations do not, however, last all 11 days. Travel through the highlands begins on 1 January, and from 6 January the trip continues in the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). This makes it quite different from spending New Year's week at a single hotel.

| Date | Itinerary |
|---|---|
| 30 December | Arrival in Quito |
| 31 December | Quito and New Year's celebrations |
| 1–5 January | Andean landscapes, cities and transfers |
| 6–8 January | Galápagos Islands |
| 9 January | Departure from Baltra |

For a broader overview of the country, its regions and climate, see our [Ecuador guide](/ecuador/). This article focuses on the specific holiday tour, its dates and the differences from a standard itinerary.

## What happens in Quito on 31 December

Ecuadorian New Year traditions centre on *Año Viejo*, a farewell to the year that is ending. In many cities, people make figures from paper, cardboard and old clothing, depicting famous characters, events of the past year or the "old year" itself. The figures are burned at midnight to symbolise the end of that chapter. Another recognisable custom involves the humorous "widows of the old year". These traditions are also described on Ecuador's official tourism portal.

The tour's 31 December programme begins with a sightseeing visit to Quito. It covers the historic districts and churches, followed by a trip to [Mitad del Mundo](/ecuador/place/mitad-del-mundo/), the monument marking the equator. A visit to the nearby [Intiñan Museum](/ecuador/place/intinan-museum/) is also planned. The city tour introduces everyday Quito before the festive evening.

After returning to the hotel, guests have free time, followed by **a New Year's dinner with traditional music and dancing**. Breakfast and dinner are specified for that day. These are concrete included elements of the programme; the itinerary does not promise participation in every city procession, a particular effigy exhibition or access to a special performance stage. Local celebrations may change from year to year, so the existence of an Ecuadorian tradition should not be mistaken for an admission ticket to a particular public event.

## Early January: lakes, volcanoes and historic cities

After the festivities, the route leaves the capital. On 1 January, the group travels through Tigua towards [Quilotoa Crater Lake](/ecuador/place/quilotoa-lake/) and then to [Baños](/ecuador/place/banos/). The itinerary describes the Quito–Quilotoa drive as approximately 3.5 hours and Quilotoa–Baños as another 3.5 hours. Much of New Year's Day is spent on the road, so it would be misleading to describe it as an entirely free day of relaxation.

On 2 January, the programme continues to waterfalls near Baños and then on to [Riobamba](/ecuador/place/riobamba/). Individual sites in the area include [Agoyán](/ecuador/place/agoyan-waterfall/), [Manto de la Novia (Bridal Veil)](/ecuador/place/manto-de-la-novia-waterfall/) and [Pailón del Diablo](/ecuador/place/pailon-del-diablo-waterfall/). Each actual visit depends on the programme for that excursion day: a site's appearance elsewhere on the website does not mean a separate paid transfer to it is included.

On 3 January, the itinerary passes through [Chimborazo Reserve](/ecuador/place/chimborazo-reserve/) and [Ingapirca](/ecuador/place/ingapirca/) before arriving in [Cuenca](/ecuador/place/cuenca/). Nature and history meet along this route: Chimborazo's mountain ecosystem is very different from Ingapirca's archaeological heritage. The fourth of January is devoted to Cuenca, while 5 January includes [Cajas National Park](/ecuador/place/cajas-national-park/), a cocoa-related experience and the journey to [Guayaquil](/ecuador/place/guayaquil/).

This combination of stops is well suited to travellers interested in more than just New Year's Eve and keen to discover different parts of mainland Ecuador. Be prepared for altitude changes and a busy transfer schedule. A Russian-speaking guide accompanies the group on this section, except for the first airport transfer, for which an English-speaking driver is specified.

## Galápagos after New Year: which islands are included

On 6 January, the group flies to [Baltra](/ecuador/place/baltra-island/) and transfers to [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/). The island's highlands offer a chance to see giant land tortoises in their natural habitat. Unlike the city walks around New Year, these visits take place within a specially protected natural area, where access and wildlife observation are subject to national park rules.

On 7 January, the itinerary includes a boat excursion to [Bartolomé](/ecuador/place/bartolome-island/), with swimming, volcanic scenery, time by the water and snorkelling. On 8 January, **one of two alternatives** is scheduled: [North Seymour](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) and [Bachas Beaches](/ecuador/place/bachas-beaches/), or [South Plaza](/ecuador/place/south-plaza-island/) and [Punta Carrión](/ecuador/place/punta-carrion/). The chosen option is confirmed after booking; it would be incorrect to promise that the group visits both islands that day.

These excursions are not automatically included in every New Year's tour to Ecuador. They are part of this specific [11-day "All of Ecuador" itinerary](/ecuador/tour/complete-ecuador-new-year/). An English-speaking guide is specified for the Galápagos, so it is not accurate to assume continuous Russian-speaking accompaniment throughout all 11 days without confirming this separately.

**The natural sites are more than a backdrop to the festivities.** Visitors must keep their distance from animals, never feed them and follow authorised guides' instructions in protected areas. Travellers primarily interested in island wildlife can compare [nature and wildlife tours in Ecuador](/interests/wildlife/tours/ecuador/); this New Year's itinerary combines the wildlife experience with history and the highlands.

## What is included and which expenses are separate

This is a group tour for **up to 15 participants**. Russian-speaking guiding is provided on the mainland, and English-speaking guiding on the Galápagos; some transfers are handled by drivers who speak other languages. Hotel names and rates are listed on the [New Year's tour page](/ecuador/tour/complete-ecuador-new-year/), together with meals and included entrance tickets.

It is particularly important to distinguish the cost of the land and island programme from separate payments. The published tour lists the following as **not included**: international flights, medical insurance, the Guayaquil–Galápagos–Quito or Guayaquil flight, the Galápagos National Park entrance fee, tips and personal expenses. The quoted guideline for the flight is **USD 515 per person**, and the park fee is **USD 200 per person**. Check the details and amounts against the itinerary when arranging the trip, as neither item is included in the main price.

Before travelling, confirm the current domestic flight arrangements, the location of your international departure and the required documents. **"A tour including the Galápagos" and "all flights included" may sound similar but mean very different things.** Flights and the park fee are separate in this itinerary, so prices should not be compared with other packages without considering what each includes.

## How much time is spent celebrating, exploring nature and travelling

Of the 11 days, only **31 December** is devoted to celebrating New Year. Arrival and an introductory evening are planned for 30 December; an active journey begins on 1 January. Broadly speaking, the time is divided as follows:

| Trip section | Main focus |
|---|---|
| Quito, 30–31 December | History and New Year |
| Andes, 1–5 January | Quilotoa, waterfalls, Chimborazo |
| Galápagos, 6–8 January | Tortoises, islands, the sea |
| 9 January | Return and departure |

Families with children, older travellers and anyone who finds altitude or long transfers challenging should look closely at travel times and walking options for each day. Snorkelling and boat outings depend on sea conditions, and travel between islands takes time. Extra charges and specific restrictions are set out in the tour description, not necessarily in general destination guides.

It is the schedule that makes this an event-focused trip. If you can travel on other dates and are more interested in the Andes, the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/) and Ecuadorian culture, compare the [complete Ecuador tour catalogue](/ecuador/tour/) with our [cultural and historical itineraries](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/ecuador/). The key distinguishing feature of the New Year's itinerary is **31 December in Quito followed by a journey across Ecuador starting on the very first day of the new year**.

## Current itinerary in the catalogue

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_ves_ekvador_na_novyj_god}}

The table draws its details from the current tour programme. Visiting the Galápagos is part of the prepared itinerary, but the included island excursions, separately purchased flights and national park fee must all be considered together, without assuming that every expense is covered.

## Frequently asked questions about the Ecuador New Year's tour

### Where exactly do guests celebrate New Year?

In [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/). The schedule for 31 December includes city sightseeing, visits to sites associated with the equator, and then a festive dinner with music and dancing. This is not a New Year's cruise around the Galápagos: the island section begins only on 6 January.

### When is the tour, and how long does it last?

The stated dates are **30 December 2026 to 9 January 2027**, lasting 11 days and 10 nights. It is a group itinerary for up to 15 participants. Confirmation of availability and conditions depends on booking the specific departure.

### Are the flight to the Galápagos and national park admission included?

No. Both are listed separately among the exclusions. The indicated guideline is USD 515 per person for the domestic flight and USD 200 for the park fee. Check these amounts against the tour conditions before booking.

### Can we visit both North Seymour and South Plaza?

For 8 January the itinerary offers **one alternative**: [North Seymour](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) with Bachas, or [South Plaza](/ecuador/place/south-plaza-island/) with Punta Carrión. The route choice is confirmed separately. Both islands cannot be promised on the same day.

### Is there a Russian-speaking guide throughout the itinerary?

Russian-speaking guidance is specified on the mainland and English-speaking guidance on the Galápagos. Some transfers use English- or Spanish-speaking drivers. The language of assistance varies by stage of the journey.

### What makes this different from a standard Galápagos trip?

The New Year's celebration in Quito on 31 December, followed by a sequence of mainland stops from Quilotoa to Cuenca. This itinerary combines a cultural event with an extensive sightseeing tour of Ecuador. For a trip focused mainly on marine wildlife, compare [Ecuador's wildlife tours](/interests/wildlife/tours/ecuador/).

## How to choose a festival tour based on the actual itinerary

**Start by finding the day you are travelling for in the itinerary.** A tour labelled "Rio Carnival" might feature the main competitive samba-school parades, the separate Champions' Parade, or a Carnival evening combined with sightseeing. "New Year in Brazil" can also mean very different trips: several days in Rio without domestic flights, or celebrating midnight on Copacabana before setting off on a much longer journey across the continent.

Our [events and festivals guide](/interests/events-and-festivals/) introduces the celebrations themselves. Here the aim is different: **to compare available Ada Tours itineraries by the event they actually include and what happens before and after it**. Our selection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. As well as departures built around a festival, there are combined tours where the event occupies only part of the programme.

| If your priority is | Compare these details |
|---|---|
| Rio Carnival | Parade date and admission ticket |
| New Year's Eve | Where you will be at midnight |
| Day of the Dead | Cities visited and evening excursions |
| Candelaria | The festival day in Puno |
| Several countries | Flights and road transfers |
| Rest after the celebration | Nights without scheduled excursions |

You can devote a few days to a single festival or use it as the starting point of a much larger trip. Shorter itineraries generally allow more time in one city. Longer journeys add natural and cultural highlights in other regions, but involve more travel.

## Rio Carnival: a short stay, Iguazu Falls or the beaches

If your priority is the evening performance and discovering [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), start with the [5-day Champions' Parade tour](/brazil/tour/brazil-rio-carnival-champions-parade/). According to the published programme, it includes four nights in the city, visits to Sugarloaf Mountain and Corcovado, a free day and the main Sambadrome event. **Carnival admission and return transfers between the hotel and the Sambadrome are included.** Of the tours listed here, this is the most straightforward choice for watching the show without changing hotels several times.

The [7-day "Champions' Parade and Iguazu" tour](/brazil/tour/rio-champions-parade-waterfalls/) adds the waterfalls after Carnival. Following three nights in Rio, guests spend three nights around [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), exploring the cascades from the Brazilian and Argentine sides, including the [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) area. Admission to the parade and the return transfer from the Sambadrome are included. **The Rio–Iguazu–Rio domestic flight is explicitly excluded.** This makes a significant difference to the overall budget compared with the five-day itinerary.

Day of the Dead, or Día de Muertos, is a Mexican tradition for remembering loved ones who have passed away. According to UNESCO, it brings together indigenous customs and the Christian calendar. International recognition belongs to this living community tradition, not to a single parade or city show.

[Mixquic](/mexico/place/mixquic/) is a district of Mexico City where Day of the Dead traditions are closely connected to the local cemetery. Families decorate graves and gather around them. Ethnographic accounts describe *alumbrada*, a ceremony in which candlelight accompanies remembrance and symbolically illuminates the way for souls.

### What happens at the Feast of Our Lady of Candelaria?

For example, in February 2026 the "Dances in Costume" competition and the subsequent parade were held later than 2 February.

It is therefore important to match a ticket labelled "Candelaria" with **the specific event and date**. Day six is dedicated to the festival, and day seven to Lake Titicaca. This schedule may be too tight for anyone hoping to attend more than one dance competition or parade. Choose based on **the exact festival calendar**, not simply on the name "Candelaria" in the tour title.

After Puno, there are no further festivals on the itinerary: sightseeing continues through Colca, Arequipa and the southern coast. ## When to travel and what to plan for Candelaria in Puno

Candelaria takes place in February, when rain is possible around Puno. Pack rain protection for street processions and warm clothing for the evenings. At high altitude, the daytime sun can be strong even when it is cloudy. If your journey is tied to several festival days, allow some flexibility for transport and possible schedule changes.

[Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) are approximately **3,800 metres** above sea level. [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) is also over 3,300 metres. During the first days after arriving at altitude, avoid excessive exertion and alcohol, and pay attention to sleep and how you feel. Continuing to ascend when altitude-sickness symptoms appear can be dangerous; deterioration requires medical assessment and, when necessary, descent.

The 13-day itinerary begins with Lima, Cusco and the Sacred Valley before travelling to Puno. This sequence allows some time for gradual exposure to higher elevations, although it **does not in itself guarantee complete acclimatisation**. If you have experienced altitude problems before, discuss the itinerary and preventive measures with a doctor before travelling.

There are organisational considerations, too: major festivals in Puno attract numerous dance groups and spectators. Hotel reservations, a suitable place to watch the performances, the return journey afterwards and the day's compatibility with Andean transfers all matter. When booking, agree on an actual event, date and included services rather than an abstract promise to "attend the festival".

## Frequently asked questions about festival tours in Peru

### Can I choose a tour devoted to a Peruvian festival only?

Yes. The [13-day Candelaria itinerary](/peru/tour/peru-inca-empire-candelaria-festival/) focuses on the celebration in Puno and other Peruvian landmarks. It does not require a visit to Carnival in Brazil. Departure dates for the specific season and the main dance-event date need to be agreed separately.

### Do all festival tours in this catalogue attend events in Peru?

No. Some begin with Carnival or New Year's Eve in Rio and include Peru later in the route. Check where the celebration takes place and how many days you will spend in Peruvian cities.

### When is Candelaria celebrated in Puno?

In February, with the central religious date on **2 February**. Dance competitions and large processions may take place on other days. To attend a particular performance, you need the current organisers' schedule and the ticket for that specific event.

### Does the 13-day tour include a Candelaria ticket?

The published inclusions list **festival admission and transfers**. The particular event, sector and viewing location are not specified, so they should be established when confirming the dates.

### Can I combine Candelaria and Machu Picchu on one trip?

Yes. The 13-day itinerary visits [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) before the festival day in Puno, then continues through southern Peru. The combination works provided your actual departure falls on the required festival date.

### Are domestic flights included in all New Year's tours?

No. On the [15-day Brazil–Peru journey](/multi-country/tour/brazil-peru-new-year/), domestic flights are listed as additional expenses. On the [five-country group New Year's journey](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-new-year-group-tour-19-days/), they are listed as included. Compare the specific services in each programme.

### Which should I choose for the festival itself: Peru or Brazil?

Choose [Candelaria in Puno](/peru/tour/peru-inca-empire-candelaria-festival/) for religious processions, folk dancing and Andean traditions. For a large samba-school parade or a New Year's night on an ocean beach, consider [Brazil's event-focused itineraries](/interests/events-and-festivals/tours/brazil/). These are different celebrations, with different dates and forms of participation.
